title: Derived tensor-Hom adjunction with a bimodule and retained scalars
statement:
Let $S\to B$ be a homomorphism of commutative rings. Use the ordinary module derived categories $D(S),D(B)$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], with derived tensor [lem-pc-derived-tensor-second-factor-functor] and Hom [def-pur-derived-internal-hom]. Let $E\in D(B)$, $X\in D(B)$, and $V\in D(S)$. Regard $E$ as a $B$-$S$ bimodule by restriction along $S\to B$. Write $J_E(V)\in D(B)$ for derived $S$-linear Hom from $E$ to $V$ with $B$ acting by precomposition: it is represented by $\operatorname{Hom}_S^\bullet(E^\bullet,I^\bullet)$ for a representative $E^\bullet$ of $E$ and a K-injective representative $I^\bullet$ of $V$, and $(b h)(e)=h(be)$. This is independent of representatives. With $U:D(B)\to D(S)$ the restriction functor, there is a natural isomorphism in $D(S)$
$$U R\operatorname{Hom}_B(X,J_E(V))\ \cong\ R\operatorname{Hom}_S\bigl(U(X\otimes_B^{\mathbf L}E),V\bigr).$$
It induces the tensor-Hom adjunction on morphism sets by taking $H^0$, with evaluation as counit. In particular all these comparisons remain compatible with restriction to any ring $K\to S$. No flatness of $B$ over $S$, perfectness of $E$, or boundedness of $V$ is assumed.

source.place: Tags 09LN (lemma-tensor-hom-adjunction, differential graded clause) and 09LT (lemma-tensor-hom-adjoint); ordinary commutative rings in degree zero, with the S-linear internal-Hom enhancement. The displayed enhancement follows from their chain adjunction using a K-projective B-model of X and a K-injective S-model of V.

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-algebraic-shriek-derived-hom-adjunction]. Its coinduction K-injectivity and normalized B-Hom model comparison prove that derivedBimoduleHomModel is an isomorphism. Reuse its chain isomorphism T, including both coordinate formulas; no new K-flat resolution of E is needed.

In the native closed derived category [def-pur-derived-internal-hom], expand bimoduleClosedCurry as internal uncurrying followed by precomposition with the canonical braiding. Mathlib ihomCurryIso and internalHom.mapIso show it is invertible. Uncurry its naturality equation, use evaluation naturality in both Hom variables, and apply braiding naturality. Compose with the natural enriched coinduction isomorphism to obtain the comparison natural isomorphism and E-naturality.

Apply [lem-trf-derived-coinduction-enriched-class]. Naturality of θ in the first variable and curry-prime precomposition extend the identity/counit equality to every g:X→CV. Uncurrying the global class of the closed currying map identifies it with the class of inverse braided evaluation; symmetry of the specified derived braiding [lem-asd-derived-category-symmetric] identifies the two tensor orders. The composite adjunction homEquiv formula then yields exactly the displayed H0 square. Postcomposition with the comparison isomorphism is a bijection, and curryHomEquiv-prime composed with the inverse adjunction homEquiv is a bijection; cancellation gives the required bijectivity.

Expand the counit of the composite adjunction and of the left-adjoint isomorphism. It is U of inverse braided closed evaluation followed by the coinduction counit, precisely derivedBimoduleEvaluation. Restriction along K→S preserves isomorphisms by functoriality. Apply that functor to the proved H0-square and counit equalities to obtain every restriction clause.

theorem derived_bimodule_tensor_hom (f : S →+* B) :
    (∀ (E : CochainComplex (ModuleCat.{u} B) ℤ)
        (I : CochainComplex (ModuleCat.{u} S) ℤ) [I.IsKInjective],
      IsIso (derivedBimoduleHomModel f E I)) ∧
    (∃ T : ∀ (E : CochainComplex (ModuleCat.{u} B) ℤ)
        (I : CochainComplex (ModuleCat.{u} S) ℤ),
        ((restrictScalars f).mapHomologicalComplex (.up ℤ)).obj
            (CochainComplex.moduleHomComplex E ((coinductionComplexFunctor f).obj I)) ≅
          CochainComplex.moduleHomComplex
            (((restrictScalars f).mapHomologicalComplex (.up ℤ)).obj E) I,
      (∀ (E : CochainComplex (ModuleCat.{u} B) ℤ)
        (I : CochainComplex (ModuleCat.{u} S) ℤ) (n p q : ℤ) (h : p + n = q)
        (z : (CochainComplex.moduleHomComplex E
          ((coinductionComplexFunctor f).obj I)).X n) (x : E.X p),
        (((T E I).hom.f n z).v p q h) x =
          (coinductionEvaluation f I).f q ((z.v p q h) x)) ∧
      (∀ (E : CochainComplex (ModuleCat.{u} B) ℤ)
        (I : CochainComplex (ModuleCat.{u} S) ℤ) (n p q : ℤ) (h : p + n = q)
        (z : (CochainComplex.moduleHomComplex
          (((restrictScalars f).mapHomologicalComplex (.up ℤ)).obj E) I).X n)
        (x : E.X p) (b : B),
        (coinductionEvaluation f I).f q
            (b • (((T E I).inv.f n z).v p q h) x) = (z.v p q h) (b • x))) ∧
    (∀ E : DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{u} B),
      ∃ θ : derivedBimoduleHomLeft f E ≅ derivedBimoduleHomRight f E,
        ∀ (X : DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{u} B)) (V : DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{u} S)),
          θ.hom.app (op X, V) = derivedBimoduleComparison f E X V) ∧
    (∀ (E E' X : DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{u} B))
        (V : DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{u} S)) (a : E ⟶ E'),
      (restrictScalars f).mapDerivedCategory.map
          ((ihom X).map ((MonoidalClosed.pre a).app ((derivedCoinduction f).obj V))) ≫
          derivedBimoduleComparison f E X V =
        derivedBimoduleComparison f E' X V ≫
          (MonoidalClosed.pre ((restrictScalars f).mapDerivedCategory.map (X ◁ a))).app V) ∧
    (∀ (E X : DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{u} B)) (V : DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{u} S)),
      Function.Bijective (fun g : X ⟶ (derivedBimoduleHom f E).obj V ↦
        bimoduleScalarUnit f ≫
          (restrictScalars f).mapDerivedCategory.map (MonoidalClosed.curry' g)) ∧
      ∀ g : X ⟶ (derivedBimoduleHom f E).obj V,
        bimoduleScalarUnit f ≫
            (restrictScalars f).mapDerivedCategory.map (MonoidalClosed.curry' g) ≫
            derivedBimoduleComparison f E X V =
          MonoidalClosed.curry' (((derivedBimoduleAdjunction f E).homEquiv X V).symm g)) ∧
    (∀ (E : DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{u} B)) (V : DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{u} S)),
      (derivedBimoduleAdjunction f E).counit.app V = derivedBimoduleEvaluation f E V) ∧
    (∀ (K : Type u) [CommRing K] [HasDerivedCategory.{u} (ModuleCat.{u} K)] (k : K →+* S)
        (E X : DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{u} B)) (V : DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{u} S)),
      IsIso ((restrictScalars k).mapDerivedCategory.map (derivedBimoduleComparison f E X V)) ∧
      (∀ g : X ⟶ (derivedBimoduleHom f E).obj V,
        (restrictScalars k).mapDerivedCategory.map
            (bimoduleScalarUnit f ≫
              (restrictScalars f).mapDerivedCategory.map (MonoidalClosed.curry' g) ≫
              derivedBimoduleComparison f E X V) =
          (restrictScalars k).mapDerivedCategory.map
            (MonoidalClosed.curry'
              (((derivedBimoduleAdjunction f E).homEquiv X V).symm g))) ∧
      (restrictScalars k).mapDerivedCategory.map
          ((derivedBimoduleAdjunction f E).counit.app V) =
        (restrictScalars k).mapDerivedCategory.map (derivedBimoduleEvaluation f E V))
lean.note: J_E is constructed as derived coinduction followed by native internal Hom. Its representative comparison and evaluation-at-one chain isomorphism retain precisely the precomposition B-action. The enriched comparison is constructed from closed currying and the already normalized enriched coinduction comparison. H0 is represented by maps from the derived unit R[0], with the actual ring-unit map for restriction. The statement uses the existing ordinary-module closed K-flat structure, through the landed coinduction definition interface and the normalized enriched-coinduction theorem; no copied internal Hom or tensor definition and no new hypotheses.
